meta.flash_ceiling_move_260820_a7w: OPERATOR RULING (quick task 260820-a7w): BASE-01's board-identity figure moves too, while its growth anchors stay frozen -- a NARROWING of, not an exception to, the re_anchor_note's rule against a third re-anchor. WHAT MOVED: the three avr_targets.*.flash_total figures, from 32256 / 32384 / 28672 to 32768 on all three targets, plus each flash_free derived by subtraction (flash_total - flash_used, NOT measured -- the cold build logs do not print flash_free): uno 7432 -> 7944, uno328pb 7510 -> 7894, leonardo 1766 -> 5862. Mechanism: this quick task's `board_upload.maximum_size = 32768` override in platformio.ini on all three AVR envs, plus zero_bootloader_reserve.py's `env.BoardConfig().update("bootloader.size", 0)` pre-script, which zeroes the MiniCore builder's 384 B urclock-bootloader subtraction on uno328pb specifically (without it, an INI override alone leaves that one target's reported ceiling unchanged). Origin: quick task 260820-a7w. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: flash_used stays pinned at 24824 / 24874 / 26906 and ram_used at 1573 / 1579 / 2014 on uno / uno328pb / leonardo respectively -- the growth axis this file exists to anchor is untouched, so every forward delta measured against it is unchanged at +306 B flash / +2 B RAM (the same figures scripts/baseline/size_baseline.json's own meta.deltas_vs_base01 records). ram_total, ram_free, the native_envs block and the warnings block are all byte-identical to the previous commit. WHY THIS IS NOT A RE-ANCHOR: flash_total is a board-identity invariant, not a growth measurement -- it names what the silicon can hold, not how much of it this firmware tree uses. The board's ceiling genuinely moved, deliberately, in the same quick task that moved the live baseline's own flash_total (scripts/baseline/size_baseline.json). The growth-laundering this file's own re_anchor_note warns against is a movement of flash_used against a stable ceiling to hide accumulated growth behind a moved reference point -- that did NOT happen here: flash_used did not move by even one byte, on either axis, in either file. A future reader must not cite this edit as precedent for moving the growth anchor; only the board-identity figure is licensed to move, and only when the actual silicon ceiling changes. WHY IT WAS DONE AT ALL: leaving BASE-01's flash_total at the old, bootloader-reduced figures would make compare_avr_policy_merge05 report "flash_total baseline=... observed=... (board or framework moved)" on all three targets against EVERY future real cold log, permanently, since the live tree's ceiling had genuinely and permanently moved. A gate that is red-by-design for a reason that will never resolve is how genuine regressions get ignored -- operators stop reading a gate that never goes green. Moving BASE-01's flash_total in lockstep keeps `--policy merge05` a USABLE gate rather than a permanently red one. CROSS-REFERENCE: scripts/baseline/size_baseline.json is the live record whose flash_total moved in the SAME quick task (see its own flash_ceiling_move_260820_a7w meta note for the parallel record); the five MERGE-05 band/exemption literals in scripts/check_size_baseline.py (MERGE05_UNO_CLASS_FLASH_BAND=64, the leonardo 0 B must-not-grow band, MERGE05_DEFECT_FIX_EXEMPTION_BYTES=96, MERGE05_PAGE_SIZE_SEAM_EXEMPTION_BYTES=210, MERGE05_PAGE_SIZE_SEAM_RAM_EXEMPTION_BYTES=2) are all untouched, and check_size_baseline.py itself is not modified by this quick task.
meta.native_inventory_axis_phase158: Phase 158 Plan 05 (LAND-03, OD-3): the four native_envs integers -- native.cases, native.succeeded, native_nodevtools.cases, native_nodevtools.succeeded -- moved from 141 to 184 on both entries (suites stays 17 on both; all_passed stays true). This is a THIRD axis, distinct from the two already recorded above: the growth axis (avr_targets.*.flash_used, avr_targets.*.ram_used), which stays frozen and is untouched by this edit, and the board-identity axis (avr_targets.*.flash_total), already licensed to move with cause by flash_ceiling_move_260820_a7w. This is a test-inventory axis: a frozen inventory count is monotonically invalid, because tests only accumulate -- the firmware's native suite only ever gains cases across phases, it never loses one, so a count fixed at a past phase's figure is guaranteed to go stale, not merely liable to. Cause of the original mismatch: BASE-01 was last touched for its native_envs block at its Phase 124 genesis (141 cases, 17 suites) and was never updated as later phases (through Phase 157) added native cases to the live suite. This drift is NOT caused by this milestone (v1.33): this milestone's own size-reduction diff (Phase 158 plans 02-04, jsmntok_t narrowing plus the cold re-record) touches zero files under test/native/avr/ -- the 141-to-184 gap accumulated entirely across Phases 124 through 157, before this milestone began. Declined alternative: making the case count a floor under --policy merge05 (failing only when the observed count drops below the recorded one) is more semantically honest but changes compare_native's gate behaviour, needs a new fixture pair plus a planted negative case, and widens this landing phase beyond its scope -- recorded as declined, not attempted.

envs_agree_note: native and native_nodevtools report byte-identical {cases: 141, suites: 17, all_passed: true} pairs. Measured reason: no test file under test/native/avr/ references DEV_TOOLS or CMD_DEV_* anywhere, so no suite compiles a conditional RUN_TEST case under -D DEV_TOOLS; both environments' test_filter blocks in platformio.ini carry the same 17 entries. Consequence for Phase 124: MERGE-06's wording ('pio test -e native and -e native_nodevtools report the BASE-01 case and suite counts') is satisfiable exactly as worded against this baseline. No amendment to MERGE-06 should be requested — D-04's feared live risk (the two envs legitimately diverging) did not materialise.

warnings.counting_command: pio test -e <env> 2>&1 | grep -cE 'warning: *"[^"]+" +redefined'  # macro-redefinition count; grep -cE 'warning:' for the total (identical on both native envs: 360 == 360, i.e. every warning on native is a macro redefinition, none is any other kind)
warnings.note: The 360 macro-redefinition warnings on each native env are a characterised pre-existing count, present on beta at 5c9160a before any v1.23 work, caused by each suite's own test/native/avr/<suite>/avr/pgmspace.h host shim defining 8 macros (PSTR, memcpy_P, pgm_read_byte, pgm_read_dword, pgm_read_ptr, pgm_read_word, strcpy_P, strlen_P) which ArduinoFake's own .pio/libdeps/native/ArduinoFake/src/arduino/pgmspace.h then redefines across 45 translation units -- 8 x 45 = 360, verified by per-macro breakdown (45 occurrences each). It is not a regression and not damage. Deduplicating those 17 suite-local shims would touch 17 suite directories, breaching this phase's 'no firmware code moves' boundary; that remediation (RESEARCH Option B) was considered and rejected by the operator in favor of Option A: an exact-zero rule on the three AVR envs (already true) plus this watermark on the two native envs.
